about.title: Fowler Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Fowler's economy runs on agriculture, packing facilities, and the trucking that moves goods along SR-99 and Golden State Boulevard, and workers in these industries face real risks every day. When an on-the-job injury happens, California generally requires you to go through workers' compensation rather than sue your employer directly, even if someone made a mistake. But that's not always the end of the story. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to your injury, a separate third-party claim may be possible alongside your workers' comp benefits. Fowler's mix of small-scale operations and larger distribution activity near the SR-99 corridor means equipment, vehicles, and multiple contractors are often involved in a single incident. LawProactive doesn't handle your case directly, but we can connect you with an independent attorney familiar with how these overlapping claims work in Fresno County, so you understand your options before deadlines pass.

whyChoose.title: Why Fowler Workers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Understanding the Exclusive Remedy Rule
items.desc: California generally limits an injured worker to workers' comp benefits against their employer, but that rule doesn't shield third parties like equipment makers or other drivers. An independent attorney can help sort out whether a separate claim applies to your situation.

items.title: Protecting You From Retaliation
items.desc: Reporting a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days is required, and California law makes it illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for doing so. Knowing this timeline matters, especially in smaller workplaces where reporting can feel uncomfortable.

items.title: Watching the Two-Year Clock on Third-Party Claims
items.desc: If a negligent third party contributed to your injury, that separate claim typically must be filed within two years. Missing this deadline can close off compensation that workers' comp alone doesn't cover.

items.question: I was hurt on a farm job outside Fowler. Can I still file a claim?
items.answer: Yes, workers' comp generally applies regardless of where within Fresno County the job site is located, including agricultural operations outside city limits. If equipment, a contractor, or another vehicle was involved, a third-party claim may also be worth exploring. An independent attorney can help you understand which route fits your situation.

items.question: My employer says I can't sue them for my injury. Is that true?
items.answer: In most cases, yes, workers' compensation is the exclusive remedy against your employer even if they were careless. However, that rule doesn't prevent claims against negligent third parties like equipment manufacturers, subcontractors, or other drivers. It's worth having an independent attorney look at the specifics.

items.question: My work injury happened in a vehicle accident near SR-99. Does that change anything?
items.answer: It might. If you were driving for work purposes and another driver caused the crash, you could have both a workers' comp claim and a separate third-party injury claim against that driver. Given that SR-99 and nearby corridors see a steady number of reported injury collisions each year in Fowler, this situation isn't unusual, and an attorney can help you sort out both paths.
